ideas.title: Carve a log, launch it, hop in
ideas.nearest: Chipping a stone to change its note
ideas.critique: This is the first time the hull idea closes the loop the earlier rounds lacked. The player's own adze cuts make the hull, and its buoyancy and righting moment come from that mesh, so the boat really is theirs and the ten seconds between carving and testing make a game. The voxel chipping reuses the chip stone's recipe, so the new part is the water test. If the hop-in arc and the slide off the beach look scripted, or the marching-cubes hull looks blobby up close, the film loses the strong part.

ideas.title: A clay dam the water wears
ideas.critique: This is the shallow-water stream from rounds 1 and 2 with a real step added. Excess-shear erosion lets the water carve the player's clay back, so the material keeps two histories and the patching race is a loop people return to. A Ritter check plus an erosion law is honest physics. The making is pressing a height layer, so it pushes the big goal less than a carved object would, and a clay layer drawn as a heightfield can look like a sinking grey block unless the notch is drawn well.

ideas.title: Sun prints of the friends
ideas.critique: Using the path tracer itself as the exposure, with soft shadows from the sun's disc and a ghost where a friend fidgets, is a clever use of RayMakie that no game engine has. The cyanotype law is real but simple. What it gives the player is placing things and waiting, and the payoff is a blue still, so it risks reading as one more stylised picture of the island, close to the woodcut. A fidgety friend's ghost is the clip-worthy part.

ideas.title: Lay a campfire that catches
ideas.critique: Compared with round 2 this has a real step: a 1-D char front through each stick's radius, flame height from heat release, view-factor radiation from the real stack, and flames as an emissive volume. That moves it past sticks changing colour. A glowing hot thing lighting its surroundings at dusk is still the hot-glass form again, and lumped air-limiting by packing is the weakest link. The charred sticks the next morning, burnt on one side, are the part that keeps what was done.
